steps.label: The false fruit part
lines: In cashew the PEDICEL of the flower becomes
fleshy and juicy and forms the false fruit -
steps.why: The asked fact is one word: the pedicel (the flower stalk). It swells into the juicy cashew apple, which is not the real fruit.
common_mistakes: Writing thalamus. The thalamus makes the apple's false fruit; in cashew it is the pedicel.
steps.memory_tip: The cashew apple is a swollen stalk - pedicel.
steps.margin_note: Pedicel is the mark; cashew apple names the structure.

steps.label: The true fruit

lines.text: The true fruit is the cashew nut, which

lines: develops from the ovary and hangs below the
steps.why: Completing the pair - false fruit from the pedicel, true fruit (the nut) from the ovary - shows the definition of false fruit is understood.
common_mistakes: Calling the juicy part the fruit and the nut a seed. The nut IS the fruit; the seed is inside it.
steps.memory_tip: Juicy stalk above, true nut below.
steps.margin_note: The ovary-to-nut line completes the two marks.
